key_insight: Ho³⁺-activated double-perovskite nanocrystals exhibit room-temperature intrinsic optical bistability through cross-coupled photon avalanches, without an optical cavity.
engineering_relevance: These materials could enable high-contrast optical switching, photonic memory, and multiplexed sensing; the abstract does not address AI or solar-cell performance.
method: Use low-phonon-energy double-perovskite hosts to reduce nonradiative losses.
Drive coupled excited-state reservoirs through a cross-coupled photon avalanche.
Probe the mechanism with time-resolved luminescence and visible-emission measurements.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports double-rise luminescence supporting coupled reservoirs, room-temperature switching contrast up to 46 dB, and bistability across multiple visible lines, crystal sizes, and host compositions.
watch_item: Device-level switching speed, endurance, and required pump power remain unspecified in the abstract.
paper_title: Cross-coupled photon avalanche drives room-temperature intrinsic optical bistability
